claim_boundary: C020 registers twenty-four attacks. A499 decisively destroys H128; all other results narrow or preserve the three surviving algorithmic descendants and inherited routes.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the number of continuation-complete residual classes may be exponential
attacks.method: Use E_n(X,Y)=AND_i(x_i<->y_i). Assigning X=a leaves Y=a; each of the 2^n residuals is separated from every other by the future continuation Y=a.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a two-valued Tear may appear polynomial by storing only SAT versus UNSAT
attacks.method: Observe that extracting the correct decision-only Tear for an arbitrary residual is exactly the SAT decision problem and therefore cannot serve as an independent construction.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: finite structural summaries may define continuation-complete classes
attacks.method: Exhibit opposite-label formulas with equal implemented unsigned scopes, sign profiles, variable marginals, primal graph, components and recognized XOR inventory.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: SAT-equivalent quotient classes may omit information needed to reconstruct witnesses
attacks.method: Require common future continuation behavior and witness recovery, then apply the equality-family residuals whose unique Y continuations encode all n bits.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the universal policy statement may merely rename P=NP
attacks.method: Require executable transition rules, independently checkable certificates and an explicit polynomial bound on every charged resource.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: JANUS Tear may have no nontrivial exact realizations
attacks.method: Verify component-parity Tears for explicit Tseitin families and preserve the boundary that the correct algebraic language is supplied by the family.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a policy may depend on visibly affine or XOR syntax
attacks.method: Apply the bijective nonlinear encoding x=a, y=b XOR (a AND c); the contradiction remains but the visible relation is non-affine.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: one bounded-width clause-Tear language may serve as a universal policy
attacks.method: Exhaustively saturate the odd-charge K4 Tseitin contradiction: width three is incomplete while width four is required even on the finite fixture.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the selected gadget may not satisfy the lifting theorem interface
attacks.method: Exhaust all free coordinates and target outputs to verify MAJ3 is 1-stifling; also verify both output fibres are non-affine.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Policy-0T may remain inside the first explicit quadratic occurrence envelope
attacks.method: Run Policy-0T on MAJ3-lifted odd K4 Tseitin and stop at recursive call 4N^2+1.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: destructive unit propagation and learned clauses may not yield a legal Resolution proof
attacks.method: Audit the implementation and require stable clause IDs, resolution parents, unit reasons, restrictions and branch-combination records.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: local resolution passes may hide superlinear proof depth
attacks.method: Charge exact parent depths and bound branch plus unit assignments by N; the recurrence remains a proof obligation rather than an assumption.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: exact residual memoization may be treated as free ordinary Resolution sharing
attacks.method: Compare Policy-0A with the formula-caching FC/CC framework; cache reuse is a separate inference and is not automatically p-simulated by Resolution.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: unique residual hashes may account for all cache cost
attacks.method: Count recursive calls, branch edges and memo hits separately; K4 fixtures have thousands of incoming cache contexts beyond unique states.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Policy-0A may already fit a known caching system with a ready lower bound
attacks.method: Map exact residual lookup plus local learned clauses against FC, FCW, FCWS and CC; no complete classification theorem is obtained.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the Res(⊕) MAJ3 theorem may apply directly across caching
attacks.method: Check the theorem statement and proof-system premise; it applies to Res(⊕), not to the unclassified Policy-0A caching calculus.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a common low-treewidth quotient may be inferred from the existence of a compact Tear language
attacks.method: H128 is destroyed by exponentially many continuation classes, so compact all-state Tears cannot supply the missing H127 quotient theorem.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: global charge quotient language may generalize to arbitrary SAT residuals
attacks.method: Separate family-specific Tseitin parity from the false universal continuation quotient using H128.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: local twins may forbid every compact global certificate
attacks.method: One parity bit per component distinguishes the inherited Tseitin charge layouts despite exact bounded-local equality.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: connectedness may leave the original XOR modules syntactically obvious
attacks.method: The neutral bridge removes naive connected-component parity; a module-aware Tear now requires certified or polynomially discovered semantic decomposition.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a lower bound against Policy-0T may be misreported as a lower bound against all H106 compilers
attacks.method: Record that H130 concerns one solver/proof policy and does not establish the H106 transduction factorization theorem.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Policy-0T lifting may solve the broader high-treewidth quotient route
attacks.method: Separate proof-complexity lower bounds for one policy from H119's universal output-factorization requirement.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Tear policy lower bounds may be confused with Extended-Frege rewrite lower bounds
attacks.method: Keep C020 within SAT search and Resolution/Res(⊕); no equivalent-circuit endpoint or Lipschitz potential is produced.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: all forms of computational sharing may inherit the fixed-gadget Circuit-Frege upper bound
attacks.method: Formula caching shares whole residual decisions and is not the transparent fixed-gadget composition controlled by H117.
